root_cause.text: In the igb driver's `igb_down()` teardown path, NAPI shutdown was ordered incorrectly by calling `napi_synchronize()` before `napi_disable()`, so an AF_XDP zero-copy RX poll loop that kept returning full budget in `igb_clean_rx_irq_zc()` never cleared `NAPI_STATE_SCHED`, causing `napi_synchronize()` to wait forever.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that after abrupt AF_XDP zero-copy app termination, "`igb_clean_rx_irq_zc()` repeatedly returns the full budget, preventing `napi_complete_done()` from clearing `NAPI_STATE_SCHED`," and that "`igb_down()` calls `napi_synchronize()` before `napi_disable()` ... `napi_synchronize()` spins waiting for `NAPI_STATE_SCHED` to clear, which never happens"; the patch removes `napi_synchronize()` and performs `napi_disable()` first.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that after abrupt AF_XDP zero-copy app termination, "`igb_clean_rx_irq_zc()` repeatedly returns the full budget, preventing `napi_complete_done()` from clearing `NAPI_STATE_SCHED`," and that "`igb_down()` calls `napi_synchronize()` before `napi_disable()` ... `napi_synchronize()` spins waiting for `NAPI_STATE_SCHED` to clear, which never happens"; the patch removes `napi_synchronize()` and performs `napi_disable()` first.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable NAPI before clearing the queue mapping in igb_down(), removing the redundant synchronize call and ensuring shutdown happens in the correct order.
intent_record.what: In igb_down(), the order of two operations inside the q_vector loop was changed: the call to napi_synchronize(&adapter->q_vector[i]->napi) was removed, napi_disable(&adapter->q_vector[i]->napi) was moved earlier, and igb_set_queue_napi(adapter, i, NULL) was moved to execute after napi_disable().
intent_record.how: At runtime, each queue vector's NAPI instance is now disabled before clearing the queue-to-NAPI association, relying on napi_disable() to quiesce and synchronize NAPI processing instead of doing a separate napi_synchronize() first. This prevents the queue mapping from being cleared while NAPI could still be active and removes a redundant synchronization step.

grouping_result.intent: Disable NAPI before clearing the queue mapping in igb_down(), removing the redundant synchronize call and ensuring shutdown happens in the correct order.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the teardown ordering in igb_down() by disabling NAPI before queue cleanup and removing the pre-disable synchronize, matching the root cause of napi_synchronize() hanging when NAPI_STATE_SCHED never clears.

candidates.rationale: This is the directly vulnerable call: it waits for NAPI completion before NAPI is disabled. If AF_XDP zero-copy RX keeps the poll loop rescheduling with full budget, NAPI_STATE_SCHED is never cleared and this synchronize can block indefinitely.
This call was ordered after napi_synchronize(), embodying the teardown ordering bug. NAPI needed to be disabled first to stop further scheduling before any wait for completion.

This statement also occurred before napi_disable(), contributing to the incorrect shutdown sequence described by the fix intent, though it is less directly responsible than the premature napi_synchronize() call.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the directly vulnerable statement. It waits for NAPI completion before NAPI is disabled in igb_down(), so if AF_XDP zero-copy RX keeps the poll loop rescheduling and NAPI_STATE_SCHED never clears, this call can block indefinitely.
This statement being placed after napi_synchronize() embodies the teardown ordering bug. NAPI needed to be disabled first to prevent further scheduling before any synchronization/wait step.

Author: Carolyn Wyborny <carolyn.wyborny@intel.com>

    igb: Fix possible panic caused by Rx traffic arrival while interface is down
    
    This patch reorders disabling napi and irqs during igb_down.
    This is done to avoid possible panic's found in other Intel drivers
    when Rx traffic arrives while interface is going down.
    
    Signed-off-by: Carolyn Wyborny <carolyn.wyborny@intel.com>
    Tested
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the full relevant teardown ordering in `igb_down()`. In this commit, the code does `igb_irq_disable(adapter);` and then, for each q_vector, calls `napi_synchronize(&(adapter->q_vector[i]->napi));` before `napi_disable(&(adapter->q_vector[i]->napi));`. The root cause states the vulnerability is the incorrect order of calling `napi_synchronize()` before `napi_disable()` in `igb_down()`, because a poll loop can keep `NAPI_STATE_SCHED` set and make `napi_synchronize()` wait forever. That exact vulnerable construct is present here: `napi_synchronize(...)` precedes `napi_disable(...)` inside the loop. Therefore this function contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix. Although this commit reorders IRQ disabling relative to NAPI handling, it does not implement the needed fix of disabling NAPI before synchronizing.
